column7: 2026-11-06: bytes.format shows '1024KB' near unit boundaries because toFixed rounds up after the unit is chosen (index.js lines 112-113). Fix direction agreed with the user: truncate (floor) to decimalPlaces instead of rounding, so no unit bump. NO code changes yet: finance still has to sign off the wording on the billing page. Don't edit until the user says finance approved.

2026-11-06: Capacity-alerts display rule from ops (user, 2026-11-06): never show less than real usage, so round UP to the shown precision (1048575 -> 1MB, 1025 -> 1.01KB, 2047 -> 2KB). This is the opposite of the billing rule (truncate), which is billing-specific, so it must not become bytes.format's default. Plan only so far, no code changes; ops are still reviewing alert thresholds. My own proposals (not yet agreed): opt-in 'rounding' option, scaled-integer ceil, promote unit when the ceil reaches 1024, round away from zero for negatives.

2026-11-06: bytes.format now truncates (Math.trunc on scaled value) instead of toFixed rounding; finance approved on 2026-11-06. Existing tests that expected round-up (1.5kb dp0 -> 2kb, 1.05kb dp1 -> 1.1kb) were changed to truncated values. Other billing-displayed numbers must also truncate.
